title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit / Range Bank 2 (Extended)
shortDescription: Secondary exhaust solenoid Bank 2 out of range.
fullDescription: Secondary exhaust solenoid Bank 2 out of range. The secondary fuel and exhaust families share PCM driver pairs; one shorted solenoid often triggers neighbor codes.
safetyImpact: Severe over- or under-fuel can damage pistons or cause stall on freeway.

causes.cause: Leaking injector seat raising rail demand
Sensor signal wire shorted to ground or 5V

fixSteps.title: Compare desired vs actual rail pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Graph desired and actual rail pressure during a snap throttle. Anything more than 5 bar of error during load is a hard fail.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Smell the engine bay for fuel and pressure-test the rail with engine off. A drop in static pressure flags a leaking injector or regulator.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: 5V reference and clean ground must be present at the rail-pressure sensor. Signal voltage should rise smoothly with key-on, engine-running.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump or sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If actual pressure is wildly off and the sensor is good, replace the high-pressure pump. Always torque rail fittings to spec to prevent leaks.

faq.q: Will sea-foam fix this?
faq.a: No additive can reseat a leaking injector or rebuild a worn HPFP. Mechanical repair is required.

faq.q: Why does it crank long when hot?
faq.a: Vapor lock in the rail or a leaking injector bleeds residual pressure on hot soak, lengthening crank time.

title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low (Extended)
shortDescription: Fuel pump driver feedback voltage below the threshold.
fullDescription: Fuel pump driver feedback voltage below the threshold. Secondary fuel-pump circuits are usually PWM driven by a dedicated module; blown driver fuses are a common nuisance failure.
safetyImpact: Fuel pressure or boost faults can cause stall or sudden power loss.

causes.cause: Worn fuel pump motor / low pressure

fixSteps.title: Measure fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Tee in a gauge or read PCM-reported rail pressure. Compare cranking, idle, and WOT pressure against spec.

fixSteps.title: Test pump driver duty
fixSteps.instruction: Most modern pumps run on PWM. The driver module's duty cycle should rise with demand; flat duty implies a control fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector and grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rear seat or access panel and inspect the pump connector for heat damage. Voltage-drop both pump-supply and pump-ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump or driver module
fixSteps.instruction: If pressure is low and duty is high, replace the pump assembly. If duty is fixed at zero, replace the driver module.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep driving?
faq.a: Lean conditions can damage the catalytic converter. Park and tow if pressure is below spec.

faq.q: Do I need a fuel filter too?
faq.a: If the pump failed and the filter is more than 60k miles old, replace both — debris can clog a new pump fast.

title: Engine Overboost Condition (Extended)
shortDescription: Boost pressure has exceeded the protect threshold.
fullDescription: Boost pressure has exceeded the protect threshold. Boost overshoot is often a stuck wastegate or a leaky vacuum line to the wastegate actuator.
safetyImpact: Fuel pressure or boost faults can cause stall or sudden power loss.

causes.cause: Stuck wastegate / VGT vanes carboned up
Cracked charge-air pipe causing boost leak

fixSteps.title: Smoke-test the charge-air system
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize the intake tract to 10-15 psi with a smoke machine. Any visible smoke at couplers, intercooler, or charge pipes is the leak.

fixSteps.title: Actuate the wastegate / VGT

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Performance (v4)
shortDescription: Regulator cannot maintain commanded pressure (alt path).
fullDescription: Regulator cannot maintain commanded pressure (alt path). The secondary fuel and exhaust families share PCM driver pairs; one shorted solenoid often triggers neighbor codes.
safetyImpact: Loss of pressure or temp data drives wide fuel-trim correction or limp mode.

causes.cause: Leaking injector seat raising rail demand
Sensor signal wire shorted to ground or 5V

fixSteps.title: Compare desired vs actual rail pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Graph desired and actual rail pressure during a snap throttle. Anything more than 5 bar of error during load is a hard fail.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Smell the engine bay for fuel and pressure-test the rail with engine off. A drop in static pressure flags a leaking injector or regulator.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: 5V reference and clean ground must be present at the rail-pressure sensor. Signal voltage should rise smoothly with key-on, engine-running.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump or sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If actual pressure is wildly off and the sensor is good, replace the high-pressure pump. Always torque rail fittings to spec to prevent leaks.

faq.q: Will sea-foam fix this?
faq.a: No additive can reseat a leaking injector or rebuild a worn HPFP. Mechanical repair is required.

faq.q: Why does it crank long when hot?
faq.a: Vapor lock in the rail or a leaking injector bleeds residual pressure on hot soak, lengthening crank time.
